title: Rigby to Host House Committee Hearings
raw_text:
Rigby to Host House Committee Hearings
October 7, 2026
HARRISBURG – A pair of state House committees will be calling Cambria County home this month during events hosted by state Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Camrbia/Somerset). Both hearings are open to the public.
This Friday, Oct. 9, the House Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee will hold an informational hearing beginning at 10 a.m. in Patton at the Cambria County Fire School, 292 Ott Road. The purpose of the meeting will be to discuss funding and access to firefighter training, recruitment and retention efforts across the state.
“As a former volunteer fireman, I can definitely speak to the challenges faced by our volunteer fire companies,” Rigby said. “Costs associated with firefighting are rising while the number of volunteer emergency responders is falling. We’re in the midst of a critical situation that will only get worse and threaten public safety if we don’t find answers.”
Then on Thursday, Oct. 15, the House Republican Policy Committee will gather in Cresson Township at Mount Aloysius College, 7373 Admiral Peary Highway, for a hearing titled “The Impact of New DEP Requirements.”
“We’ll be examining the Department of Environmental Protection’s proposed revisions to Pennsylvania’s biosolids permitting process,” added Rigby. “The department wants to address potential farm field and groundwater pollution by implementing monitoring and tiered restrictions in wastewater treatment systems that would prevent Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) “forever” chemical contamination in biosolids which are used as fertilizer.”
Questions about this or any state government issue should be directed to Rigby’s Cresson office at 814-886-1055, his Ferndale office at 814-536-9818, or his Somerset County office at 814-509-6942.
Representative Jim Rigby
71st Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

September 25, 2026
HARRISBURG
– State Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambria/Somerset) invites residents of the 71st Legislative District to join him in Windber for “Coffee and Conversation” on Friday, Oct. 2, from 10 to 11:30 a.m. at Marinelli Place,

title: Local Project Grants Totaling Nearly $2 Million Announced by Langerholc, Rigby
raw_text:
Local Project Grants Totaling Nearly $2 Million Announced by Langerholc, Rigby
September 15, 2026
HARRISBURG –
State Sen. Wayne Langerholc Jr. (R-35) and Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambria/Somerset) are proudly announcing more than $1.9 million in Local Share Account (LSA) funding that is being awarded to 17 projects in Cambria and Somerset counties.
“These awards will allow communities to address critical structural needs, enhance public resources, and implement targeted upgrades that strengthen local operations,” said Langerholc.  “I was proud to work with Rep. Rigby to help ensure this funding was directed back to Cambria County, providing resources that enable local entities to support local residents.”
“Sen. Langerholc and I are more than happy to work with local government officials and bring these critical projects to fruition,” Rigby added. “We’re proud to partner with them in making investments in community needs and law enforcement equipment and addressing safety and health concerns.”
The list of projects is as follows:
•	Cambria County - $279,227
for baseball field and facility improvements at Mount Aloysius College.
•	Cresson Borough - $76,800
for the purchase of a skid steer loader.
•	Cresson Township - $49,365
for the purchase of a new police vehicle and $139,925 for purchasing of a new backhoe.
•	Ferndale Borough - $52,650
for replacement of a retaining wall along Plainfield Ave.
•	Geistown Borough - $84,510
for the purchase of a police SUV.
•	Lilly Borough Water Authority - $87,750
for the purchase of a backup generator to be used in Washington Township.
•	Loretto Borough - $25,360
for the purchase and deployment of license plate readers, body cameras, in-vehicle cameras and computers and printers for both the police station and police cars; and $189,731 to purchase three cardiac monitor/defibrillators for use by the Cresson Area Ambulance Service.
•	Portage Borough Municipal Authority - $29,400
for the purchase of a cold cut planer attachment for use in removing asphalt and concrete surfaces with precision; and $90,090 for system improvements that will ensure water quality and operational efficiency within the distribution system.
•	Reade Township - $137,604
for the purchase of a dump plow truck.
•	Reade Township Municipal Authority - $130,000
for the rehabilitation of two water tanks and $50,855 for purchasing a truck.
•	Richland Township - $157,950
for the purchase of playground equipment at Highland Regional Park and $229,739 to purchase a truck for use in plowing snow.
•	Scalp Level Borough - $114,642
for the purchase of a new truck to be used in Windber Borough.
•	Stonycreek Township - $98,138
for the purchase of an excavator.
The Local Share Account (LSA) program provides funding for projects that promote economic development, community improvement and public interest projects across Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Rigby to Host Monthly Veterans Outreach Service

Rigby to Host Monthly Veterans Outreach Service
August 7, 2026
HARRISBURG
-  State Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambria/Somerset) invites veterans who live in the 71st Legislative District to take advantage of a service he’ll be providing each month.
“American Legion Department Service Officer Stephen Schott will meet with area veterans on the third Wednesday of each month, beginning Wednesday, Aug. 19,” said Rigby. “This is an opportunity for the men and women who serve and have served our country to ask questions and discuss programs that are available to them.”
Officer Schott is trained to provide expert assistance at no cost to veterans and their families. He’s available to answer questions regarding survivor benefits, discuss access to veteran-related resources and provide support for service-related concerns.
Officer Schott will visit Rigby’s Ferndale district office, which is located at
1021 Ferndale Ave
., Johnstown, between 2-4 p.m.
To make an appointment for Wednesday, Aug. 19, please call the office at 814-536-9818.
The 71st Legislative District consists of the following municipalities: in Cambria County, the townships of Adams, Allegheny, Chest, Clearfield, Cresson, Dean, Gallitzin, Munster, Portage, Reade, Richland, Stonycreek, Summerhill, Washington and White; and the boroughs of Ashville, Cassandra, Chest Springs, Cresson, Ferndale, Gallitzin, Geistown, Lilly, Loretto, Portage, Sankertown, Scalp Level, South Fork, Tunnelhill and Wilmore; and in Somerset County, the townships of Ogle and Paint and the boroughs of Paint and Windber.

title: Rigby to Host Cyber Crime Awareness Class
raw_text:
Rigby to Host Cyber Crime Awareness Class
July 28, 2026
HARRISBURG – State Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambia/Somerset) is again partnering with members of the Saint Francis University faculty to conduct a Cyber Crime Awareness Class on Tuesday, Aug. 4, from 6-8 p.m. at the Oakland Volunteer Fire Company, 1741 Bedford St., Johnstown.
Anyone planning to attend the seminar should register in advance by either calling Rigby’s office at 814-886-1055 or visiting his website,
RepJimRigby.com
, and clicking on the “Events” tab.
“An informed consumer is an empowered consumer, and the cyber criminals we’ll be discussing  are hoping you fail to recognize the warning signs of a scam and fall prey to their attempts at disrupting your personal life,” said Rigby. “This class is free and designed to help you stay informed, stay alert and stay safe online.”
The seminar will be led by three members of the university’s faculty:
•	Dr. Kevin Slonka, associate professor and cybersecurity director in the Computer Science Department. He has decades of industry experience and award-winning research in cyber security.
•	Michael Zambotti, assistant professor in cybersecurity. His area of expertise is open-source intelligence, incident response and risk management.
•	Dr. Mark Buckwalter, associate professor of criminal justice. He is a retired federal agent with 27 years of law enforcement experience in corrections, probation, parole and mental health services.

title: Rigby Approves of Education Funding in State Budget
raw_text:
Rigby Approves of Education Funding in State Budget
July 13, 2026
HARRISBURG – When it comes to support for Pennsylvania school students, state Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambria/Somerset) agrees with the 2026-27 state budget.
“The compromise that the House and Senate agreed to would adequately fund our public schools and keep intact both the Educational Improvement Tax Credit (EITC) and Opportunity Scholarship Tax Credit (OSTC) programs, which support school choice,” said Rigby, a member of the House Appropriations Committee. “It’s a win for Pennsylvania students and their families and gives them the flexibility they deserve in choosing which course of learning is best for them.”
The school districts that Rigby represents would receive the following increases in combined Basic Education, Special Education and Ready to Learn Block Grant funding:
Cambria County:
•	Cambria Heights - $276,849 (2.2%)
•	Ferndale Area - $290,221 (3.4%)
•	Forest Hills - $789,712 (4.7%)
•	Greater Johnstown -  $3,296,854 (8.2%)
•	Penn Cambria - $712,011 (5.3%)
•	Portage Area - $343,613 (3.8%
•	Richland -  $451,942 (7.7%)
Clearfield County:
•	Glendale - $378,295 (4.5%)
Somerset County:
•	Conemaugh Township Area - $310,841 (3.6%)
•	Windber Area - $701,273 (5.4%)
Questions about this or any state government issue should be directed to Rigby’s Cresson office at 814-886-1055, his Ferndale office at 814-536-9818, or his Somerset County office at 814-509-6942.

title: Rigby to Host Safe Driving Course for Senior Citizens
raw_text:
Rigby to Host Safe Driving Course for Senior Citizens
May 3, 2026
HARRISBURG
- State Rep. Jim Rigby (R-Cambria/Somerset) is partnering with Seniors for Safe Driving to offer two Mature Driver Improvement courses in the coming months.
“These events are very well attended and usually generate a waiting list, which is why we’ve already scheduled a second class,” said Rigby. “They are taught solely in a classroom setting and provide a good test of the rules of the road for anyone who may have lost confidence behind the wheel.”
The courses Rigby is co-hosting are scheduled as follows:
•
Wednesday, May 13, Windber Recreation Park and Pool,
60 Rec Road, Windber
(noon to 4 p.m.).
•
Wednesday, Aug. 12, Richland Township Fire Department’s Solomon Run fire hall,
176 Mt Airy Drive, Johnstown
(5-9 p.m.).
The PennDOT-approved course is designed for seniors aged 55 and older at a cost of $17. Completing the course will earn participants a minimum 5% discount on auto insurance premiums over a three-year period.
Anyone interested in registering for the course may do so by either calling 1-800-559-4880 or going online to
SeniorsForSafeDriving.com
.
Questions about this or any state government issue should be directed to Rigby’s Cresson office at 814-886-1055, his Ferndale office at 814-536-9818, or his Somerset County office at 814-509-6942.
